heroBody: A good gaming monitor is the single biggest competitive edge you can buy in 2026: 165Hz to 240Hz refresh, 1ms response and adaptive sync turn a mid-range GPU into a noticeably smoother experience than a premium GPU on a 60Hz panel. In Singapore, the gaming monitor market is dominated by LG UltraGear, Samsung Odyssey, ASUS ROG and Gigabyte Aorus, with BenQ and AOC filling the budget end. This page pulls live Singapore listings from BuyWhere's catalog every few minutes so the price on each card is what authorised retailers and marketplace sellers are actually charging today.

highlightSectionTitle: What changed with gaming monitors in 2026

highlights.title: 27-inch 1440p is the new standard
highlights.body: Two years ago, 1080p 144Hz was the sweet spot; in 2026, 27-inch 2560x1440 at 165Hz or 180Hz is the mainstream gaming choice because it pairs with mid-range GPUs (RTX 4060-4070 tier) to deliver high frame rates without the GPU bottleneck that 4K creates. If you have not upgraded your monitor in three or more years, 1440p 165Hz is the step to take.

highlights.title: OLED is finally in the gaming line-up
highlights.body: LG and Samsung's 27-inch OLED gaming monitors (240Hz, 0.03ms response) have dropped into the mainstream premium band in Singapore after debuting at the very top of the price range in late 2024. OLED brings perfect blacks and zero motion blur to gaming. The trade-off is burn-in risk for static HUD elements in long sessions; if you play one game for hours, IPS is still the safer pick.

highlights.title: Adaptive sync is now standard
highlights.body: Both FreeSync Premium Pro (AMD) and G-Sync Compatible (NVIDIA) are now built into every gaming monitor worth buying, so the AMD-vs-NVIDIA choice no longer dictates the monitor. What still matters is the FreeSync Premium tier (low frame-rate compensation, low latency) versus basic FreeSync; cheaper panels without the Premium tier stutter when the frame rate drops below the refresh rate floor.

adviceSectionTitle: How to pick a gaming monitor in Singapore without overspending
advicePoints: Match your monitor to your GPU first. A RTX 4060 wants 1440p at 165Hz; a RTX 5080 wants 4K at 144Hz or 1440p at 240Hz. Buying a 4K 240Hz monitor for a mid-range GPU wastes money on a screen you cannot drive.
Prefer IPS over VA for esports. VA panels have higher contrast for movies but slower pixel response, which smears in fast motion. IPS is the safer pick for Valorant, CS2, Apex and Overwatch.
Check the USB-C input. If you dock a laptop or a recent MacBook for portable gaming or work, USB-C with Power Delivery above 65W means you can use one cable for video, data and charging.

Buy local warranty if you can afford it. Parallel-import gaming monitors from Sim Lim Square are cheaper but LG, Samsung and ASUS Singapore's three-year warranty does not apply. A panel replacement outside warranty costs more than the savings.

Test the stand height and tilt. A 27-inch monitor at desk level needs at least 100mm of height adjustment to align with your eye line. A monitor arm (VESA 100x100) is a worthwhile add-on if you swap monitors.
faqSectionTitle: Gaming monitors in Singapore — common questions

faqs.question: Is a 1440p gaming monitor worth it over 1080p in Singapore?
faqs.answer: Yes, for any GPU above the RTX 4060 tier. 1440p at 165-180Hz gives a meaningful jump in both sharpness and motion clarity over 1080p 144Hz. If your GPU is below an RTX 4060, the frame rate cost of 1440p is real and 1080p 144-165Hz remains the smart pick.

faqs.question: What size gaming monitor should I buy in Singapore?
faqs.answer: 27 inches for desktop viewing at 60-80cm; 32 inches for desks 80cm deep or for 4K where the higher pixel density helps. Anything above 32 inches at standard viewing distance makes competitive gaming harder because your eyes need to track further across the screen.

faqs.question: Is an OLED gaming monitor worth the premium in Singapore?
faqs.answer: If you play a mix of games and care about HDR and motion clarity, yes. If you play one game for hours a day with a static HUD, the burn-in risk over 3+ years is real and an IPS monitor is the safer pick. The price gap between 27-inch OLED and IPS has narrowed to roughly 30-40 percent in 2026.

faqs.question: When is a gaming monitor cheapest in Singapore?
faqs.answer: Mid-year (June to July) and year-end (November to December) sales at Courts, Harvey Norman and Best Denki typically drop gaming monitor prices by 15-25 percent. Shopee Mall and LazMall official stores match within a day or two and stack platform vouchers on top.

categoryIntro.heading: Why gaming monitor prices in Singapore swing so widely
categoryIntro.body: Gaming monitors in Singapore are sold by authorised retailers like Courts, Harvey Norman and Best Denki at full warranty prices, marketplace sellers on Shopee Mall and LazMall with mixed warranty status, and parallel-import shops in Sim Lim Square and Funan at meaningful discounts. Authorised retailers carry Singapore local sets; parallel imports skip the local distributor markup but lose the manufacturer's Singapore warranty. The spread for the same panel can reach 25-30 percent, which is why a static 'best price' table goes stale within days and why this page reads live listings instead.
